title: Randomised trial evaluating mifamurtide in combination with standard chemotherapy in patients with high-grade osteosarcoma at high risk of relapse.
official: SARCOME 13 / OS2016 - A Multicentre, Randomised, Open-label, Phase 2 trial of mifamurtide combined with post-operative chemotherapy for newly diagnosed high risk osteosarcoma patients (metastatic osteosarcoma at diagnosis or localised disease with poor histological response)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the impact on efficacy (event-free survival, EFS) of mifamurtide administered during 36 weeks as add-on treatment to post-operative chemotherapy, compared to post-operative chemotherapy alone, in first-line treatment of patients >2 years and ≤ 50 years with high-risk osteosarcoma (metastatic at diagnosis or localised with poor histological response to pre-operative chemotherapy).
conditions: Patients ≤50 years old with high-risk osteosarcoma (defined as metastatic osteosarcoma at diagnosis or localised osteosarcoma with poor histological response) after pre-operative chemotherapy and surgery of the primary tumour and lung metastases (if applicable).

interventions.name: MEPACT 4 mg powder for concentrate for dispersion for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. At diagnosis : All newly diagnosed, biopsy-proven, high-grade osteosarcoma, whatever the initial extension of the disease
2. For the randomisation : Osteosarcoma classified as high risk because of at least one risk factor
3. For the randomisation : Pre-operative chemotherapy
4. For the randomisation : Screening laboratory values must meet the following criteria (using CTCAE v5) and should be obtained within 7 days prior to randomisation
5. For the randomisation : Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test (minimum sensitivity 25 IU/L or equivalent units of HCG) done within 7 days prior to randomisation
6. For the randomisation : Provision of dated and signed written informed consent for the randomised trial prior to any study specific procedures, sampling and analyses.
7. For the randomisation : Patient fit to undergo protocol treatment and follow-up
8. For the randomisation : Affiliation to a social insurance regimen
9. At diagnosis : Age >2 years and ≤50 years
10. At diagnosis : Normal haematological, renal, cardiac and hepatic functions
11. At diagnosis : Planned neoadjuvant chemotherapy
12. At diagnosis : Written informed consent from patients and/or their parents/guardians before enrolment and any study-related procedure
13. At diagnosis : Affiliation to a social insurance regimen
14. For the randomisation : Patient with a histologically proven, confirmed by expert pathologists panel (before surgery at the latest), high-grade osteosarcoma
15. For the randomisation : Registered at diagnosis into the study
16. For the randomisation : Primary tumour resected after pre-operative chemotherapy
Exclusion criteria:
1. Low grade osteosarcoma, parosteal or periosteal osteosarcoma
2. Concurrent use with high-dose non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs, cyclooxygenase inhibitors)
3. Inflammatory or auto-immune disease, allergy or asthma requiring a chronic use of steroid treatment that cannot be stopped
4. Patients with positive test for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) or known acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)
5. Patients with positive tests for hepatitis B virus surface antigen (HBV sAg) or hepatitis C virus ribonucleic acid (HCV RNA) indicating active or chronic infection
6. Prior history of other malignancies other than osteosarcoma (except for basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin or carcinoma in situ of the cervix) unless the patient has been free of the disease for at least 3 years
7. Osteosarcoma with multiple metastases for whom complete removal is not expected to be feasible even after shrinkage with chemotherapy
8. Progressive disease at any site during initial pre-operative chemotherapy, confirmed before randomisation time, with exception of patients with progressive disease of the primary tumour who had a complete resection at surgery
9. Any medical condition precluding treatment with protocol post-operative chemotherapy
10. Fractional Shortening < 28% or LVEF< 50% before treatment (only for API post-operative chemotherapy) by echocardiogram or Muga scan
11. Pregnancy or breast-feeding
12. Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients
13. Concurrent use of immunodepressive treatment such as cyclosporine, tacrolimus or other calcineurin inhibitors
